title: Permission model
subtitle: rwx, chmod, SUID/SGID, sticky, chattr — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Three who: user (owner), group, other — each with r, w, x
cards.notes: Leading type char: - file, d directory, l symlink, c/b device. Ownership is UID/GID.

cards.meaning: May enter / resolve a path (cd, open a file inside)
cards.notes: On a dir: r = list names; w = create/delete/rename entries (needs x too). On a file: x = run.

cards.meaning: r=4, w=2, x=1 — three digits = user, group, other
u/g/o/a with + add, - remove, = set exactly
cards.example: chmod g=rw test.t; chmod o-r,g+w test.t
cards.notes: chmod 755 when you think in numbers; chmod g+w when you think in letters.

cards.meaning: chown sets user owner; chgrp sets group owner
cards.example: chown user:group path; chown -R user path
cards.notes: Only root can give a file to another user on typical Linux. -R is recursive.

cards.meaning: On a shared directory, only delete/rename files you own
cards.notes: Without sticky, write on the dir lets anyone unlink anyone’s file. ls -l shows t/T in other’s x slot. Extra octal digit 1.

cards.meaning: Process runs with the file owner’s effective UID
cards.notes: Classic: passwd runs as root to update /etc/shadow. Linux typically ignores SUID on scripts — binaries only. Extra octal 4.

cards.meaning: Process runs with file’s group as effective GID; on dirs, new files inherit the directory’s group
cards.notes: Useful for shared project directories. Extra octal digit 2. 4755 = SUID+755; 2755 = SGID+755; 1777 = sticky+777.
Leading 0 clears special bits (e.g. chmod 0700). Combine with the usual three mode digits.

cards.meaning: rwxr-xr-x — owner full; group and other read+execute
cards.notes: 7=rwx, 5=r-x, 5=r-x. Typical for directories and some scripts others must run.

cards.meaning: rw-r--r-- — owner read+write; everyone else read-only
cards.notes: Common for ordinary data files (no execute).

cards.meaning: Immutable — no changes, deletes, or renames until unlocked
cards.notes: Beyond rwx on ext filesystems. Unlock with -i before you edit. lsattr to inspect.

cards.meaning: Append-only — file: only append; directory: add files but not rename/delete existing
cards.notes: Other common flags: +A no atime; +s secure deletion (zero blocks on delete if FS honors it).
-R recursive; -d treat directory as a file (do not list contents). chmod = rwx; chattr = extra ext flags.

cards.meaning: World-writable shared dir where you may only throw away your own trash
cards.notes: Bob’s /tmp/bob cannot be deleted by tom when sticky is set, even if /tmp is 777.
